# Per-binding FFI overhead

<!-- Generated by `node tools/comparison/dist/perf/overhead-table.js` from the records under `results/counts/ab/`; `mise run verify:claims` fails if it drifts from them. Do not edit by hand. -->

What each binding layer adds to an operation over the Rust core, as retired user-space instructions (`instructions:u`) per operation: the median over the record's interleaved A B / B A blocks of `mise run benchmark:counts`. Arm A is the layer's driver and arm B the core's, built in the same crate and profile from `bindings/overhead/protocol.rs`; both arms' outputs are byte-identical in every record. Every cell is tier 1 on the perf matrix's gradient fixture; a batch is 16 copies through a one-worker batch encoder. Every process of every arm in every record on this page runs under `GLIBC_TUNABLES=glibc.malloc.mmap_threshold=65536`, which the record states (`settings.glibcTunables`). No wall-clock figure is recorded or claimed. Reproduce with `mise run benchmark:overhead`.

## Host runtimes

What each host runtime adds to a call, counted through its published binding. Arm A is the host's own command-line driver (the cross-language benchmark's `encode-stdin`), run under the host's counting configuration (`counts-core.ts` `COUNTING_CONFIGS`); arm B is the core driver of the native layer the host binds, counted with `--b-impl Rust` on the same cell, and both arms decode to the same RGBA bytes or encode to the same hash in every record. A host is countable where, in every one of its records, each arm's per-operation count in each of the interleaved blocks is within 1.000% of that arm's median; the check and its tolerance were fixed in issue #173 before any host was counted. The check tests that a record repeats, not that its per-operation figure is independent of the iteration count: work a process does once, part-way through the long process only (a JIT compile at its call threshold, say), is spread over the iterations, so each figure is its cell's at that record's iteration count (`settings.iterations`). Kotlin is counted in the JVM's interpreter for this reason; with C1 at its call threshold its decode counted about 12% more per call at 500 iterations than at 2,000. In the interpreter a smaller dependence remains, unexplained: arm A counts 0.5% more per decode at 500 iterations than at 2,000, 0.9% more per 64×64 encode at 200 than at 800, and 0.7% more per 512×512 encode at 20 than at 80, where the host side falls by 11.7% and, under the pinned allocator configuration below, the core (arm B) moves by 45 instructions. A counting configuration is not how the host ships: it pins the runtime's compiler tier and its collector's pacing, so a host's figure is its cost under that configuration. "Native layer" is the overhead row above for the same cell, counted against the same core binary, and "Host side" is what is left: the host's call, its marshalling and its runtime, with its CLI's bench loop. The subtraction assumes the core does the same work in every process, which is why every arm runs under `GLIBC_TUNABLES=glibc.malloc.mmap_threshold=65536`: under glibc's defaults the 512×512 encode's buffers pass malloc's 128 KiB mmap threshold, which glibc raises once the first such buffer is freed, so one process served them from its heap, zeroing them in user space, and another mapped fresh zeroed pages, and the core's allocator work differed between a host's process and the core driver's (issue #184: unpinned, the Python CLI's 512×512 host side read +26,089 against +293,855 at 64×64). Pinning the threshold turns the dynamic threshold off, so every buffer of 64 KiB or more is mapped in every process. A host side below zero is not what the host adds (the core did less work in the host's process, or the arms ran different core code), and the table refuses such a row rather than print it. A count also belongs to its revision (the line at the end names each): two records' figures compare only where they were counted on the same core binary, which `renderOverheadTable` holds a host row to against its native layer's row. The TypeScript (wasm) arm runs the core itself as wasm in V8's baseline compiler, so its figure is the whole call against native code rather than the glue alone; the glue's share is not separable by this count.

With the allocator configuration pinned, the encode's host side changes with the input size only by what the host does per pixel or per unit of the call's duration. Python's pixels cross in one `memmove` (the `uniffi-py-bytes` reduction), and its 512×512 host side is 0.7% over its 64×64 one. C# and Go pass the pixels by pointer, with no copy; their 512×512 host sides differ from their 64×64 ones by +747 (C#) and +3,623 (Go) instructions, against a core (arm B of `host-csharp-encode-512.json` and `host-csharp-encode-64.json`) that counts 31.1 times the instructions at 512×512 (106,695,154 against 3,431,165). Their A − B per block also spreads more at 512×512 than at 64×64 (1,648 against 145 instructions for C#, 1,924 against 713 instructions for Go), which is what work that scales with the encode's duration rather than its input (a runtime thread counted with the process) would show. That share is not separated by this count. Kotlin's 512×512 host side is 17.4% over its 64×64 one, its 512×512 record counted at 20 iterations and its 64×64 record at 200; the difference carries the interpreter's iteration dependence above, which this count does not separate from what grows with the input.

| Host | Host side, encode 64×64 | Host side, encode 512×512 | 512×512 − 64×64 | 512×512 / 64×64 |

| C# | +1,107 | +1,854 | +747 | 1.675 |
| Go | +3,989 | +7,612 | +3,623 | 1.908 |
| Kotlin | +5,552,014 | +6,515,881 | +963,867 | 1.174 |
| Python | +293,587 | +295,531 | +1,944 | 1.007 |

## Every binding

| Binding | Native layer | Counted here | Not counted |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| C | C ABI | the whole call | — |
| C# | C ABI | the whole call, under its counting configuration (Host runtimes) | the .NET runtime (tiered JIT, concurrent collector) as it ships: its count is under the counting configuration |
| Go | C ABI | the whole call, under its counting configuration (Host runtimes) | the Go runtime (its concurrent collector, every processor) as it ships: its count is under the counting configuration |
| Kotlin/JVM | UniFFI scaffolding | the whole call, under its counting configuration (Host runtimes) | the JVM (tiered C1/C2 compilation in the background, its default collector) as it ships: its count is under the counting configuration |
| Android | UniFFI scaffolding | the native side of every call, as Kotlin/JVM | JNA and ART: they run on a device, not on the counting host |
| Python | UniFFI scaffolding | the whole call, under its counting configuration (Host runtimes) | CPython started through `uv run`, with a random hash seed as it ships: its count is under the counting configuration |
| TypeScript (wasm) | wasm-bindgen | the whole call, under its counting configuration (Host runtimes) | V8 with its optimizing tiers (Maglev, TurboFan) and background threads, which is where the wasm core runs as it ships: its count is under the counting configuration |
| Swift | UniFFI scaffolding | not measured | Swift builds on macOS only (`ci-swift.yml`); its native layer is the UniFFI row above |

## Reductions

Each reduction is byte-identical (both arms' outputs are equal in every record) and is shown by a paired count of the layer's driver after it (A) against the same driver built before it (B), each cell counted with `benchmark:overhead`'s options, `--impl` naming the driver's implementation and `--b-bin` naming the earlier build; every block of every record counts fewer instructions after it.

### `uniffi-bytes` (uniffi)

UniFFI byte arrays lifted and lowered in one slice copy instead of one push per byte (`bindings/uniffi/src/bytes.rs`); `ImageInput.rgba` lifted straight into the core's `Arc<[u8]>`. A is `bindings/uniffi/target/after/overhead_uniffi`, built at `8f78dff`; B is `bindings/uniffi/target/before/overhead_uniffi`, built at `c4b3f9e`.

| Cell | After (A) | Before (B) | Change | A/B | Record |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | --- |
| encode 64×64 | 3,740,194 | 4,345,085 | −604,891 per encode | 0.8608 | `reduce-uniffi-bytes-encode-64.json` |
| encode 512×512 | 109,515,719 | 148,266,354 | −38,750,635 per encode | 0.7386 | `reduce-uniffi-bytes-encode-512.json` |
| decode (64×64's hash) | 2,404,798 | 2,449,862 | −45,064 per decode | 0.9816 | `reduce-uniffi-bytes-decode-64.json` |
| batch of 16 × 64×64 | 59,865,164 | 69,592,248 | −9,727,084 per batch | 0.8602 | `reduce-uniffi-bytes-batch16-64.json` |

### `wasm-rgba-copy` (wasm)

`DecodeResult::rgba` returns a `Uint8Array` built from the decoded slice (`bindings/wasm/src/lib.rs`), so the pixels cross to JS in one copy instead of a clone in the wasm heap, wasm-bindgen's copy of the clone and its free. Counted through the TypeScript package's CLI under Node's counting configuration (Host runtimes), on the decode cell, the only one whose path it changes. A is `bindings/wasm/target/after/typescript/dist/encode-stdin.js`, built at `84e3338`; B is `bindings/wasm/target/before/typescript/dist/encode-stdin.js`, built at `4fd0571`.

| Cell | After (A) | Before (B) | Change | A/B | Record |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | --- |
| decode (64×64's hash) | 6,128,099 | 6,129,765 | −1,666 per decode | 0.9997 | `reduce-wasm-rgba-copy-decode-64.json` |

### `uniffi-py-bytes` (uniffi)

The Python bindings write a byte array into the RustBuffer in one `ctypes.memmove` instead of one Python loop iteration per byte, by a step `mise run cbuild:python` applies to uniffi-bindgen's output (`mise-tasks/cbuild/python`), so lowering `ImageInput.rgba` no longer runs w × h × 4 iterations per encode. Counted through the Python package's CLI under CPython's counting configuration (Host runtimes), on the encode cells, the ones whose input it writes; each arm is a package directory, run from its parent. A is the build at the record's revision; B is `bindings/uniffi/target/before/python/chromahash`, built at `32ffc24`.

| Cell | After (A) | Before (B) | Change | A/B | Record |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | --- |

| encode 512×512 | 107,091,546 | 2,829,788,079 | −2,722,696,533 per encode | 0.0379 | `reduce-uniffi-py-bytes-encode-512.json` |
